name: What the iPhone ended
description: A hand-picked view: the phones, players, cameras and plug-ins that faded once the iPhone made the phone the main computer.
author: codegrave

checkpoints.name: The iPhone arrives
checkpoints.note: Apple shows the iPhone in January 2007 and opens the App Store in July 2008. The phone, not the PC, becomes the computer most people carry.

checkpoints.name: The rivals fall
checkpoints.note: Phones built around keyboards and older systems lose ground quickly. The Nokia N95 is gone by 2009, the Flip camera and the Zune player close in 2011 and 2012, and by 2013 Nokia has dropped Symbian and the BlackBerry Curve has ended. In 2010 Steve Jobs explains why the iPhone will not run Flash.

checkpoints.name: The plug-ins fade
checkpoints.note: Browser plug-ins lose ground to HTML5. Windows Phone is given up in 2017, Flash reaches its end on 31 December 2020 and Silverlight in 2021, and in 2022 Apple stops making the iPod, the device the iPhone was first sold as a successor to.
